title: What Counts as Catering Spend When a Corporate Catering Service Agreement Closes
content:
## The basis

The spend counted toward the minimum on a closing Corporate Catering Service Agreement is taken from the agreement's own entries over the 12 months ending on the day it closes, and what is taken in depends on which kinds of entry stand in that window.

**Where cancellation charges stand raised on the agreement in the 12 months ending on the day it closes and service credits stand allowed in the same 12 months**, the spend counted is what has been invoiced in that window together with those cancellation charges and less those service credits.

**Where cancellation charges stand raised in that window and no service credit stands allowed in it**, the spend counted is what has been invoiced in that window together with those cancellation charges.

**Otherwise**, the spend counted is what has been invoiced in that window.

## Combinations

| Cancellation charges raised in the window | Service credits allowed in the window | The spend counted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | yes | invoiced, plus the cancellation charges, less the service credits |
| yes | no | invoiced, plus the cancellation charges |
| no | yes | invoiced only |
| no | no | invoiced only |

A service credit never comes off the spend counted unless a cancellation charge also stands raised in the same 12 months: the third row takes in the invoiced total alone.

## Illustration on hypothetical figures

On a hypothetical closing agreement carrying 30000.00 USD invoiced in that window, 1200.00 USD of cancellation charges raised in it and 500.00 USD of service credits allowed in it, the spend counted is 30700.00 USD. Had no service credit stood allowed in the window, it would be 31200.00 USD. Had no cancellation charge stood raised in it, the spend counted would be 30000.00 USD whether or not service credits stood allowed.
